entries.title: a Web Forms attribute is read in every form ASP.NET accepts, and a schema stays capped in every repository
entries.summary: From @outoftheblue9 (#1067). The Web Forms reader took only double-quoted attribute values, so an unquoted `runat=server` or a single-quoted `CodeFile='Q.aspx.cs'` gave a control's handler no reference and a page no edge to its codebehind; live code could read as unused. Directives, `runat`, `ID`, `On*` handlers and `<script runat>` are now read double-quoted, single-quoted and unquoted, in one pass that takes each quoted value whole. `.xsd` and `.wsdl` files stay capped in every repository: `build_consumed` with project-file advice where the index holds .NET evidence, and the new neutral kind `schema_consumer` (counted as `schema_consumer_withheld`) elsewhere, so a Java repository no longer gets .NET advice. Indexes re-parse on their next run (parser generation 20).

entries.title: jcodemunch-mcp diagnose writes one local report with no path and no repository name
entries.summary: New command: `jcodemunch-mcp diagnose` writes one JSON report to the storage directory's `diagnose` folder and prints its path. It holds server versions, each index as `index-1` with its sizes, the tool surface, the state of each installed policy, and per tool the calls, tokens returned and tokens saved. It is built from a fixed list of fields and of what each value may be, so no path or repository name can reach it; the `anon_id` is left out unless `--include-anon-id` is passed. It sends nothing. New background behaviour, disclosed in SECURITY.md: the server now keeps two local counts per tool (calls, tokens returned) in `_tool_counters.json`, on by default and sent nowhere. `"tool_counters": false` turns them off.

entries.title: a Python import written over several lines records its names, and the surface offer reaches the user
entries.summary: Two changes. A Python `from x import (...)` spread over several lines, or continued with a backslash, recorded only the names on its first line, so `find_references` and `check_references` missed every name on the lines after it. All of them are recorded now; indexes re-parse on their next run (parser generation 19). New behaviour, disclosed in SECURITY.md: an install serving the full tool list is told once, in its first successful `resolve_repo` answer, what the three-tool front door would save it per turn, with a line asking the agent to pass that on. It changes no setting, sends nothing, and writes one marker file, `surface_notice_state.json`, so it is not repeated. `jcodemunch-mcp config set surface_offer_seen true` silences it.

entries.title: the generated agent policy no longer orders the index for everything
entries.summary: The policy that `init` installs opened "Always use jCodemunch-MCP tools for code navigation. Never fall back to Read, Grep, Glob, or Bash", and required two calls before any task. On a small repository that wording costs turns the built-in tools would not. The policy now says where each route is cheaper: the index for relationships, for a large repository and for a question with no known starting point; the built-in tools on a small repository and for a file about to be edited. `resolve_repo` and `plan_turn` are conditional. A policy installed before this release is not rewritten: `jcodemunch-mcp config --check` reports that it differs, and `jcodemunch-mcp claude-md --generate --format policy` prints the current text. This is an interim change; the CHANGELOG lists what still steers to the index.
